newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola plans $1 billion investment in E. Europe.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola plans $1 billion investment in E. Europe.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co. said Tuesday the beverage giant and its bottlers plan to invest $1 billion in eastern Europe, including $100 million in both Russia and Poland in 1997.
A Coca-Cola spokeswoman confirmed remarks by company President Doug Ivester in the Hungarian daily Vilaggazdasag Tuesday, in which he clarified previously announced expansion plans.
The Atlanta-based company has already invested $1.5 billion in the countries of Central Eastern Europe, of which Hungary took $250 million, Vilaggazdasag said.
Ivester said Coca-Cola is likely to invest $50 million in Hungary in sales development and could boost the staff of its Hungarian subsidiary by up to 300 new employees.
Coca-Cola's stock rose 37.5 cents to $51.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
